title: AppSurface logical-key contract normative matrix

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: Payments:ApiKey queried with casing variants
rows.expectedOutcome: Same value and hash identity
rows.coverageNote: All four real provider harnesses include CaseIdentity and compare original/lowercase typed queries with the same expected value through ConfigProviderContractAssert.Case. The kernel test asserts equal hashes. No remaining assertion gap identified.

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: Logging:LogLevel:Microsoft.Hosting.Lifetime
rows.expectedOutcome: Three segments; final dotted segment intact

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: Payments:Api-Key and Payments:Api:Key
rows.expectedOutcome: Distinct identities/native ids

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: empty, :A, A:, A::B, controls, edge whitespace
rows.expectedOutcome: Reject with no partial key

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: null/empty array, null/invalid member, caller mutates source array
rows.expectedOutcome: Defined exceptions; successful Segments remains unchanged

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: missing/found/terminal factories with null and diagnostic combinations
rows.expectedOutcome: Only the three valid states construct

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: high provider returns terminal result
rows.expectedOutcome: No lower-provider lookup; preserve one transactional any-successful-child environment rescue; throw when no child applies

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: multiple children present and one conversion/collision fails
rows.expectedOutcome: No mutation or partial rescue; terminal patch diagnostic wins

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: same spelling twice
rows.expectedOutcome: Duplicate failure before value selection

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: exact/case-varied duplicate properties in UTF-8 tokens
rows.expectedOutcome: Token parser rejects before DOM materialization

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: colliding descendant plus unrelated sibling
rows.expectedOutcome: Exact key and ancestors terminal; unrelated sibling remains available
rows.coverageNote: Real colliding file tokens make the exact key/ancestors terminal, retain unrelated siblings, and suppress a recording lower provider through DefaultConfigManager.

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: null, empty aggregate, array, scalar/object replacement
rows.expectedOutcome: Normative replacement and missing semantics with correct provenance
rows.coverageNote: Current layering table includes scalar-to-array and array-to-scalar, empty aggregates, object merge and null-as-missing. Assertions verify replacement value, exact winner-first file origins with locations, and removal of stale object/array descendants. Latest two cases were source-inspected; their owner controls execution, and the Google run does not execute them.

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: ApiKey plus apikey
rows.expectedOutcome: Collision terminal/startup failure
rows.coverageNote: File/environment cases exercise case-varied same-layer names. Local shared harness seeds exact case-varied durable records and asserts terminal/no fallback. Google host startup registers the real module with case-only logical mapping duplicates and distinct native ids, then asserts OptionsValidationException before any client call. Google run executes its portion only.

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: exact wrapper/manual spelling registered twice
rows.expectedOutcome: Existing metadata merge; one report spelling

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: case-only or legacy/canonical spellings identify same key
rows.expectedOutcome: Startup collision with both safe spellings

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: same spelling in scoped/unscoped or ordered files
rows.expectedOutcome: Higher layer wins; both sources audited
rows.coverageNote: File layering asserts the higher replacement value and both exact file origins in winner-first order; environment diagnostic resolution asserts scoped winner and exact scoped/unscoped origins with Base/Override roles.

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: casing differs across layers
rows.expectedOutcome: Collision for affected key

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: same logical key in two providers
rows.expectedOutcome: Existing manager precedence; both sources audited
rows.coverageNote: Audit deliberately shuffles high/low provider order, asserts precedence winner and both provider sources/calls, with and without a winning environment provider.

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: declaration present/absent across casing-varied providers
rows.expectedOutcome: Declaration spelling, else winning-provider spelling; stable ordering
rows.coverageNote: Discovery arranges case-varied logical identities in shuffled high/low providers, then asserts declaration spelling when declared, winning source spelling otherwise, stable ordering, one grouped identity, and both exact source spellings.

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: two aliases in one scope
rows.expectedOutcome: Terminal collision even if values match
rows.coverageNote: Real Local file-backed alias tables use identical payloads for every canonical/historical candidate combination, including two historical aliases; collisions select no value and diagnostics omit the payload. Existing environment equal-value collision evidence is retained.

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: distinct keys encode/map to same id
rows.expectedOutcome: Options or pre-network representability failure
rows.coverageNote: Environment explicit suffix collision and Google distinct-key/same-exact-resource constructor tests both assert OptionsValidationException, satisfying the options-failure alternative. No remaining assertion gap identified.

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: Payments with Payments:Key and PaymentsArchive:Key
rows.expectedOutcome: Claim first only

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: explicit suffix configured
rows.expectedOutcome: Replaces canonical suffix in scoped and unscoped layers

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: underscore boundaries and environment-prefix counterexamples
rows.expectedOutcome: Convention rejects or maps explicitly; no two accepted keys share one full name
rows.coverageNote: Provider counterexamples A_:B, A:_B and environment-prefixed logical keys reject ambiguous conventions; explicit mapping escapes the prefix case. Generated accepted claims across three environments assert every complete scoped/unscoped native candidate has only one logical owner.

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: scoped and unscoped expected names both present
rows.expectedOutcome: Scoped wins; both sources audited

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: exact, one case-only, and two case-varied native names
rows.expectedOutcome: Resolve, casing terminal, and collision respectively on Unix/Windows fakes

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: backing variables mutate during direct/collection/patch operations
rows.expectedOutcome: One top-level resolution stays on captured snapshot; next call sees new state

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: sparse high collection indices and a large object graph
rows.expectedOutcome: Prefix index visits present candidates only; cached bind plan respects depth/cycle limits

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: unrelated native variables beside registered keys
rows.expectedOutcome: Only forward-known keys are audited; unrelated names omitted

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: explicit/generated mappings across project, id, version, and casing
rows.expectedOutcome: Exact full-resource equality collides; distinct ordinal resources do not
rows.coverageNote: Six exact ordinal resource pairs vary project, secret id, version, and casing independently. Concurrent explicit/convention reads retain independent fetches, cache values, and exact audit sources. Identical explicit resources fail before client access; overlapping explicit/convention identity is terminal. Resolved aliases and project ID/number responses retain exact returned identifiers; distinct keys converging on one concrete resource poison both requested claims. Actually unrelated resource responses remain terminal.

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: two concurrent keys attempt one resource
rows.expectedOutcome: Atomic claim is poisoned; triggering and subsequent requests are terminal
rows.coverageNote: A blocked Explicit:Key fetch overlaps distinct Payments:One claiming the same native resource. Triggering, pending, and subsequent resolutions for both keys are terminal with and without caching; audit is invalid and no extra client access occurs. The test exposed and now verifies the claim recheck at value publication. Alias response provenance is tested through the real Google adapter seam for runtime-first/audit-first calls, cache enabled/disabled, rotating uncached values and bounded resolved-name history. Audit sources remain coupled to the exact payload version without a second fetch. UTF-8, scalar, JSON and null conversion failures evict only their own generation; runtime/audit retries fetch the repaired alias version, and a controlled second resolver proves a newer cache entry survives an older conversion failure.

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: many concurrent waiters, cancellation, failure, and retry
rows.expectedOutcome: One shared fetch, cancelled waiter isolated, failed entry evicted, payloads immutable
rows.coverageNote: Cancellation of either the initiating or following blocked waiter leaves the other successful on one shared fetch. Four waiters receive one shared failure; retry fetches again and caches success. Mutated client input bytes, exposed payload copies, and returned mutable objects/arrays cannot change cached or uncached later results. Existing 32-waiter evidence is retained. Warm and cold pre-cancelled runtime/audit requests test both the exact cached key and a would-be conflicting key: caller cancellation preserves OperationCanceledException without client/claim effects; audit-only deadlines remain incomplete diagnostics. Shared live waiter cancellation evidence is retained.

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: cache/claim/audit budget exhausted
rows.expectedOutcome: Stable terminal or explicit incomplete audit; bounded memory and elapsed time

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: exact mapping under a matching convention
rows.expectedOutcome: Explicit wins for that key; full identifier retained

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: dot-only string in compatibility mode
rows.expectedOutcome: One translated identity plus replacement diagnostic

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: legacy and canonical declarations translate to same identity
rows.expectedOutcome: Startup collision; no provider traversal

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: none, canonical only, one legacy only, canonical+legacy, two legacy
rows.expectedOutcome: Missing, found, warned found, collision, collision
rows.coverageNote: Local real-file strict three-candidate and translated two-candidate tables assert every subset: missing/no notice, canonical/no notice, each legacy exact migration notice, and multiple equal-valued candidates terminal/no selected value. Environment alias evidence is retained.

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: exact --from-stored-key plus strict --to
rows.expectedOutcome: Source bypasses parsing; destination shows parsed segments, with dots literal and colons hierarchical
rows.coverageNote: New CLI theories assert source strings that fail logical grammar are forwarded exactly; destination dots stay literal and colons create displayed segments; preview calls no migration; apply forwards exact source/typed destination only after displaying preview; invalid destination fails before store creation. Test execution is pending the assigned watcher.

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: higher source returns collision/unrepresentable
rows.expectedOutcome: Stop; do not query lower providers

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: crash/failure before/after every durable transition and store mutation
rows.expectedOutcome: Resume roll-forward or stop safely; never expose/overwrite value
rows.coverageNote: Real file backend injects before/after all 17 read/commit/mutation boundaries, reopens the persisted store/journal, resumes Complete with retained migration ID/value and absent source, and checks payload-free journal/result. Reopened changed destinations stop without deleting source.

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: backend lacks lock/durable journal/confirmed operations
rows.expectedOutcome: Unsupported before Prepared; no mutation
rows.coverageNote: File backend capability rejection uses a filesystem whose operations count and throw: unsupported result before any I/O, including Prepared journal. CLI separately rejects a store lacking migration capability before operations.

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: second process/write races every journal boundary
rows.expectedOutcome: Shared lease or CAS prevents stale delete; index and journal recover together
rows.coverageNote: Independent process writer is excluded before/after each durable journal state; after lease release it succeeds and a reopened store retains both writes. Reopen/retry tests cover every mutation boundary; changed destinations preserve source, preventing stale delete.

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: same/different keys register concurrently
rows.expectedOutcome: One deterministic mapping or safe collision
rows.coverageNote: Four controlled concurrent convention resolutions register two distinct keys and their case variants, retain distinct mappings, and coalesce each identity to one fetch. An overlapping distinct-key/same-resource test proves claim poisoning. Immutable projection read evidence is retained.

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: late options, manual-only declarations, concurrent first access, and two hosts
rows.expectedOutcome: One complete immutable registry per host; no wrapper activation or partial seal
rows.coverageNote: Concurrent first access asserts one complete 64-key mixed raw/typed registry across 32 requests; read-only snapshots, late policy, manual-only setup and two-host isolation are covered. A counting/throwing discovered wrapper remains inactive through registration, registry creation and host startup.

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: translated nested attribute reaches wrapper/provider/audit
rows.expectedOutcome: Original composed spelling and origin survive without affecting equality
rows.coverageNote: Real nested attributed wrappers registered through AppSurfaceConfigModule exercise strict/translated/typed origins. Assertions track exact key instance, composed original spelling, origin, equality/hash through registry, wrapper initialization, provider request and audit; no wrapper activation before resolution.

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: external free text plus controls/oversized identifiers
rows.expectedOutcome: Manager logs only catalogued fields and escaped bounded safe identifiers
rows.coverageNote: Manager logging test supplies external sentinel prose, controls, and oversized identifiers; asserts no sentinel/newline leakage, bounded messages, and catalogued fallback code. Identifier/catalog tests assert escaping and stable bounds. Replaced incidental history, metrics, and redacted-report evidence.

rows.inputOrSourceArrangement: file, environment, notice, and renderer limits exceeded
rows.expectedOutcome: Stable value-safe failure; no partial snapshot or unbounded retention
rows.coverageNote: Actual FileBasedConfigProvider byte/count exhaustion asserts stable terminal runtime/audit status, no value or enumerable partial snapshot, and an unaffected environment. Retained tests directly assert environment snapshot failure, bounded notice retention and escaped bounded report/diff rendering.

coverageInterpretation: Coverage status describes assertion evidence in current shared source, not an assertion that current tests have executed or passed. Named methods and files are checked. verificationRuns records only actual existing run artifacts with their stated scope; source changes after a run require revalidation. This bounded refresh re-evaluated previously partial/uncovered rows and retained the other rows from earlier assertion audits.
